title: R-form a cos θ + b sin θ
examples: How do I find the value of R?
What does alpha represent in this form?
Can this method be used for other combinations?

explain.say: Today we learn to write expressions like a cos theta plus b sin theta. This is called the R-form. It makes the expression much simpler to work with.

draw.text: R-form a cos θ + b sin θ
a cos θ + b sin θ → R cos (θ - α)

explain.say: We combine the coefficients a and b into a single number, which we call R. R is always positive. We find R using the formula R equals the square root of a squared plus b squared.
Next, we find an angle alpha. This angle relates to the original coefficients a and b. We use the tangent function for this step. Remember to check the signs of a and b.
So, a cos theta plus b sin theta becomes R cos (theta - alpha). This form helps us easily find the maximum and minimum values of the expression.

items: a cos θ + b sin θ

faq.q: What is R in the R-form?
faq.a: R is the amplitude of the resulting trigonometric function. It represents the maximum possible value of the expression. You might also hear this called the amplitude.
asks: How do I find the amplitude?

faq.a: Alpha is the phase angle or phase shift of the function. It tells us how far the graph has moved horizontally. Sometimes we use the inverse tangent function to find it.

faq.q: Does R always have to be positive?
faq.a: Yes, R is defined as the positive square root of a squared plus b squared. This ensures R is always a positive number. We never use a negative value for R.

faq.q: What if one of the coefficients a or b is zero?
faq.a: If one coefficient is zero, the process simplifies greatly. For example, if b is zero, the expression is just a cos theta, and R will simply be the absolute value of a. You can still use the general formula.
asks: Does the formula still work if a is zero?

faq.q: How do I find the maximum value using this form?
faq.a: Once you have the R-form, the maximum value is simply R. This is because the cosine function itself has a maximum value of one. Therefore, R times one is R.
asks: How do I find the highest point?

facts: The R-form converts a cos theta plus b sin theta into R cos (theta - alpha).
The value of R is calculated using the formula R equals the square root of a squared plus b squared.
The maximum value of the expression is equal to R.
The angle alpha is determined using the relationship tan alpha equals b divided by a.

quiz.say: Rewrite 3 cos theta plus 4 sin theta in R-form.
quiz.show: 3 cos θ + 4 sin θ → R cos (θ - α)
quiz.why: You correctly found R using the Pythagorean identity and determined alpha using the tangent ratio.

wrong.1: This is tempting because you added the coefficients, but R must be found using the square root of the squares.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you are adding the coefficients, but R represents the hypotenuse, not the sum.
wrong.3: This is a common error because you swapped the roles of a and b when finding the angle alpha.

quiz.say: Find the maximum value of 5 cos theta + 5 sin theta.

options.say: Maximum value is 5the square root of 2 cos(0)
Maximum value is 5the square root of 2

quiz.why: Since a equals b, R is found by the square root of 5 squared plus 5 squared, which is 5√2.

wrong.0: This is a common mistake of forgetting to use the square root when calculating R.
wrong.1: This is overly complicated; you only need to find the value of R, which is the maximum.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you added the coefficients, but the maximum value is determined by R.

quiz.say: If the expression is 2 cos theta + 0 sin theta, what is R?
quiz.why: When b is zero, R is simply the absolute value of a, which is two.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the coefficient 'a' is non-zero, meaning the function has a range.
wrong.1: This incorrectly includes the cosine function when finding the constant value R.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because R must account for the full coefficient 'a' in the expression.
